correctness.rationale: The non-frame reduction, translate independence, automorphy, and Gaussian zero-density steps are the exact ingredients of the recent primary proof. The new step is a reconstructed Wronskian multiplicity lemma: for N>m, common m-th derivative zeros force Wronskian zero multiplicity at least N-m because N distinct nonnegative row orders avoiding m have total order at least N(N-1)/2+N-m. This gives (N-m)/(N delta)<=1. Irrational delta permits arbitrary N; rational p/q permits N=q, which yields q-p<=m. Stable integer shifts of the derivative window are independently verified by Fourier periodization.

value.rationale: The result turns a recent exact m=1 technique into a general arithmetic law. It unifies the Gaussian and first-Hermite cases, proves that every irrational subcritical lattice is safe for every Gaussian derivative, and confines all possible rational holes to the narrow strip q-p<=m. This sharply reduces the search space for complete frame sets and is driven by a new structural Wronskian multiplicity calculation rather than a routine substitution.
